symbols.name: B
symbols.def: The pairs whose disturbances may be correlated.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: The candidate directed backbone supplied with the graph.

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: The permitted number of directed edges outside \(T\).

symbols.name: Lambda
symbols.def: The matrix \(\Lambda\) supported on \(D\), in the convention \(X=\Lambda^{\mathsf T}X+\varepsilon\).

symbols.name: lambda_D
symbols.def: \(\lambda_D=(\lambda_{ij}:i\to j\in D)\), the nonzero-support coordinates of \(\Lambda\).

symbols.name: Omega
symbols.def: The symmetric disturbance matrix before its graph-support restriction is imposed.

symbols.name: phi_G
symbols.def: The \(\mathbb C\)-algebra homomorphism defined by \(\phi_G(\sigma_{ij})=[(I_n-\Lambda)^{-\mathsf T}\Omega(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}]_{ij}\), with every missing off-diagonal disturbance entry fixed at zero; acyclicity makes every image entry polynomial in \(R_{\mathrm{src}}\).

symbols.name: psi_G
symbols.def: The \(\mathbb C\)-algebra homomorphism extending \(\phi_G\), fixing each coordinate in \(\lambda_D\), and sending each \(\sigma_{ij}\) to its acyclic covariance parametrization.

symbols.name: d_e
symbols.def: \(d_e(G)=[K_G(\lambda_e):K_G]\) when \(\lambda_e\) is algebraic over \(K_G\), and \(d_e(G)=\infty\) otherwise.

symbols.name: A_K
symbols.def: \(A_K=S_G^{-1}(R_{\mathrm{inc}}/I_G)\cong K_G\otimes_{R_G}(R_{\mathrm{inc}}/I_G)\), the integral generic-fiber algebra obtained by inverting exactly \(S_G\) and no source-coordinate expression.

symbols.name: U
symbols.def: A maximal subset \(U\subseteq\lambda_D\setminus\{\lambda_e\}\) algebraically independent over \(K_G\).

symbols.name: CensusHandle
symbols.def: The exact small-size falsification handle specified in \(\mathrm{def:census\mbox{-}handle}\).

symbols.name: e_star
symbols.def: The first sink coefficient in the family \(G^{\star}_{k,n}\).

symbols.name: delta
symbols.def: The requested upper bound on randomized symbolic error.

symbols.name: ArithmeticModel
symbols.def: Unit-cost arithmetic over \(\mathbb Q\) and finite fields, rational arithmetic circuits in \(\sigma_{ij}\), Schwartz--Zippel testing at independently sampled field points, and exact rational reconstruction with bit complexity charged separately.

symbols.name: p_e
symbols.def: When \(d_e(G)<\infty\), \(p_e(t)\) is the monic minimal polynomial of \(\lambda_e\) over \(K_G\), represented coefficientwise by rational arithmetic circuits in \(\sigma_{ij}\).

symbols.name: Q_Ge
symbols.def: When \(d_e(G)<\infty\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\) is the output family of covariance-localization, incidence-lifting, pole, projective-leading-form, specialized-leading-coefficient, squarefreeness, and real-lifting circuits in the entries of \(\Sigma\).

symbols.name: h_Ge
symbols.def: When \(d_e(G)<\infty\), \(h_{G,e}=\prod_{q\in\mathcal Q_{G,e}}q\), with repeated nonzero factors removed.

symbols.name: N_Ge
symbols.def: \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\) is a source-parametric dominance certificate showing that the \(\lambda_e\)-projection of a positive-dimensional irreducible component of the generic covariance fiber is Zariski dense in \(\mathbb A^1_{K_G}\), and hence that \(\lambda_e\) is transcendental over \(K_G\).

symbols.name: Alg
symbols.def: The tagged algorithmic output contract specified in \(\mathrm{def:certificate\mbox{-}algorithm}\); the transcendental branch contains no \(p_e\)-dependent object.

symbols.name: Z_e
symbols.def: \(\mathcal Z_e(G,\Sigma)=\{z\in\mathbb C:\exists\Lambda\in\mathbb C^D,\ \lambda_e=z,\ F_{ij}(\Lambda,\Sigma)=0\text{ for every }i\leftrightarrow j\notin B\}\), the finite-coordinate projection of the specialization of the prime incidence ideal \(I_G\).

symbols.name: R_e
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)=\{z\in\mathbb R:\exists\Lambda\in\mathbb R^D,\ \lambda_e=z,\ F_{ij}(\Lambda,\Sigma)=0\text{ for every }i\leftrightarrow j\notin B\}\).

symbols.name: LiftCert
symbols.def: When \(d_e(G)<\infty\), a rational-univariate lifting representation, isolating interval, and exact sign data certifying whether a simple real root of \(p_e\) belongs to \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\).

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: The number of independent observational draws.

symbols.name: C_Ge
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_{G,e}\) is the connected smooth semialgebraic cell in \(\mathcal M_G\setminus\mathcal E_{G,e}\) specified in \(\mathrm{def:regular\mbox{-}cell}\), refined so that every real-root extension label is constant.

symbols.name: gamma
symbols.def: A positive uniform lower bound on distances between distinct retained roots whose existence is derived in \(\mathrm{lem:derived\mbox{-}root\mbox{-}separation}\).

symbols.name: Kappa_G
symbols.def: \(\mathcal K_G\) is a nonempty compact subset with nonempty relative interior in \(\mathcal C_{G,e}\), as specified in \(\mathrm{def:regular\mbox{-}class}\).

symbols.name: pi_G
symbols.def: A smooth nearest-point projection from a tubular neighborhood of \(\mathcal K_G\) onto its smooth covariance-model stratum.

symbols.name: J
symbols.def: \(J=|\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)|\), which is positive and constant on the selected connected regular cell.

symbols.name: r_vec
symbols.def: The increasing local labeling of \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\) on a connected regular neighborhood.

symbols.name: d_H
symbols.def: For finite \(A,B\subset\mathbb R\), \(d_H(A,B)\) is the ordinary Hausdorff distance when both sets are nonempty, \(d_H(\varnothing,\varnothing)=0\), and \(d_H(A,B)=\infty\) when exactly one of \(A,B\) is empty.

symbols.name: H_m
symbols.def: \(\mathcal H_m\) is the event that \(S_m\) lies in the projection neighborhood, every certificate circuit is valid at \(\pi_G(S_m)\), and all retained roots are matched to their population branches.

symbols.name: A_m
symbols.def: The image under the smooth root map \(r\) of a joint asymptotic confidence ellipsoid for \(\pi_G(S_m)\), with one neighborhood for each retained branch.

novel.justification: The index records a transparent departure from a supplied hierarchy: applied path diagrams often add a small number of cross-level parents to a rooted causal tree.

assumptions.condition: \(T\subseteq D\) is a rooted spanning arborescence on \(V\).

novel.justification: The condition permits arbitrary placement of a bounded number of extra parents while retaining an interpretable hierarchical backbone, including skip-level and converging-parent structures used in path analysis.

definitions.name: Tree-plus-\(k\) graph-query class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal G_{n,k}=\{(G,T,e):|V|=n,\ e\in D,\ (V,D)\text{ is acyclic},\ T\subseteq D\text{ is a rooted spanning arborescence},\ |D\setminus T|\le k\}\) for every admissible \(n\) and \(k\).

definitions.name: Generic residual fiber algebra
definitions.construction: Let \(\phi_G:R_{\sigma}\to R_{\mathrm{src}}\) send each covariance coordinate to its acyclic SEM polynomial, put \(P_G=\ker\phi_G\), extend it to \(\psi_G:R_{\mathrm{inc}}=R_{\sigma}[\lambda_D]\to R_{\mathrm{src}}\) by fixing \(\lambda_D\), and put \(I_G=\ker\psi_G=(F_{ij}:i\ne j,\ i\leftrightarrow j\notin B)\). With \(R_G=R_{\sigma}/P_G\), \(K_G=\operatorname{Frac}(R_G)\), and the exact multiplicative set \(S_G=R_{\sigma}\setminus P_G\), define \(A_K=S_G^{-1}(R_{\mathrm{inc}}/I_G)\cong K_G\otimes_{R_G}(R_{\mathrm{inc}}/I_G)\). Equivalently, the covariance saturation is \(I_G:S_G^{\infty}=I_G\); no polynomial involving a directed source coordinate is inverted.

definitions.name: Size-sensitive orientation-realization handle
definitions.construction: Freeze a coordinate transcendence basis \(U\), select square residual-Jacobian subsystems blockwise by child vertex, encode their multihomogeneous Bezout coefficients as prescribed-indegree orientation counts, and determine exactly which counts are realized in the prime incidence algebra after localization at \(S_G=R_{\sigma}\setminus P_G\), with one original edge coordinate separating all finite branches; the output is a recurrence in \(n,k\), not a guessed exponent.

definitions.name: Rooted five-node incidence handle
definitions.construction: Enumerate rooted graph-query isomorphism orbits with \(n\le5\) and \(k\le2\); for each orbit compute the characteristic-zero queried-edge elimination ideal from \(A_K=S_G^{-1}(R_{\mathrm{inc}}/I_G)\), homogenize before removing projective-infinity points, certify the affine squarefree degree by a rational univariate representation, and compare it with the prescribed-orientation coefficient. Lift the supplied modular quartic by rational reconstruction, exact substitution into \(I_G\), and verification that every inverted covariance factor lies in \(S_G\).

definitions.name: One-sink family
definitions.construction: For \(d=k+1\) and \(n\ge2k+4\), take vertices \(0,P_1,\ldots,P_d,Q_1,\ldots,Q_d,h\), directed edges \(0\to P_i\), \(0\to Q_i\), and \(P_i\to h\), supply \(T=\{0\to P_i,0\to Q_i:1\le i\le d\}\cup\{P_1\to h\}\), omit exactly \(P_i\leftrightarrow Q_i\) and every ordinary-vertex pair with \(h\), allow all other bidirected pairs, set \(e^{\star}=P_1\to h\), and append any remaining vertices as fully bidirected children of \(0\) whose tree arrows are added to \(T\).

definitions.name: One-sink family membership verification
definitions.construction: For \(d=k+1\), the displayed backbone has \(2d+1=2k+3\) directed edges on \(2d+2=2k+4\) vertices. Exactly \(d-1=k\) arrows \(P_i\to h\) lie outside the supplied backbone, and each appended vertex adds one tree edge and no excess arrow. Thus the supplied edge set is a rooted spanning arborescence, the directed support is acyclic, \(e^{\star}\in D\), and \((G^{\star}_{k,n},T,e^{\star})\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\). This is an inline support verification, not an identification target.

definitions.name: Source-integral Möbius quadratic core
definitions.construction: Expose every incoming coefficient at a vertex of indegree at least two; on the other vertices factor rank-one residual relations in the integral source field, propagate rank-two relations by Möbius maps, record every genuine pole and every identically zero-over-zero interaction, and retain the resulting degree-at-most-two equations in at most \(2k\) exposed coefficients as \(\mathsf{Core}_{G,e}\).

definitions.name: Fixed-parameter minimal-polynomial algorithm
definitions.construction: In \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\), reduce to \(\mathsf{Core}_{G,e}\), use randomized source-parameter identity tests and a coordinate-preserving generic slice, and test whether \(\lambda_e\) is algebraic over \(K_G\). If \(d_e(G)<\infty\), compute multiplication by \(\lambda_e\), descend its squarefree monic minimal polynomial to \(K_G\), and return the finite tag \((d_e,p_e,\mathcal Q_{G,e},h_{G,e})\). If \(d_e(G)=\infty\), return exactly the transcendental tag \((\infty,\mathcal N_{G,e})\), where \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\) certifies dominance of the queried-coordinate projection from a positive-dimensional irreducible generic-fiber component onto \(\mathbb A^1_{K_G}\); do not construct or return \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\) on this branch.

definitions.name: Certificate exceptional set
definitions.construction: When \(d_e(G)<\infty\), define \(\mathcal E_{G,e}=V(h_{G,e})=\{\Sigma:h_{G,e}(\Sigma)=0\}\), where \(h_{G,e}\) is the product of the nonzero covariance-localization, incidence-lifting, pole, projective-leading-form, specialized-leading-coefficient, squarefreeness, and real-lifting circuits returned by \(\mathsf A\).

definitions.name: Real extendable coordinate set
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)=\{z\in\mathbb R:\exists\Lambda\in\mathbb R^D,\ \lambda_e=z,\ F_{ij}(\Lambda,\Sigma)=0\text{ for every }i\leftrightarrow j\notin B\}\).

definitions.name: Connected regular real-model cell
definitions.construction: For fixed \(G,e\) with \(d_e(G)<\infty\), \(\mathcal C_{G,e}\) is a connected cell of a smooth semialgebraic stratification of \(\mathcal M_G\setminus\mathcal E_{G,e}\), refined by the signs used in \(\mathsf{LiftCert}\), on which the number and extendability labels of the simple real roots of \(p_e\) are constant.

definitions.name: Compact regular finite-fiber class
definitions.construction: For fixed \(G,n,e\) with \(d_e(G)<\infty\), select \(\mathcal C_{G,e}\) as in \(\mathrm{def:regular\mbox{-}cell}\) and let \(\mathcal K_G\subset\mathcal C_{G,e}\) be any nonempty compact set with nonempty relative interior in that cell.

definitions.name: Projected-covariance root-set estimator
definitions.construction: For \(d_e(G)<\infty\), if \(S_m\) lies in the tubular neighborhood of \(\mathcal K_G\), \(\pi_G(S_m)\notin\mathcal E_{G,e}\), and the returned circuits evaluate validly, set \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\{z\in\mathbb R:p_e(\pi_G(S_m),z)=0\text{ and }\mathsf{LiftCert}(z,\pi_G(S_m))\text{ accepts}\}\), retaining every accepted branch and selecting none; otherwise set \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Simultaneous branch neighborhoods
definitions.construction: For \(d_e(G)<\infty\), construct \(\mathcal A_m\) by mapping a joint Gaussian covariance ellipsoid for \(\pi_G(S_m)\) through every locally labeled component of \(r\), using the implicit derivative \(D r_j(\Sigma)[H]=-D_\Sigma p_e(\Sigma,r_j)[H]/\partial_t p_e(\Sigma,r_j)\).

statements.statement: The homomorphism \(\psi_G:R_{\mathrm{inc}}\to R_{\mathrm{src}}\) is surjective, \(I_G=\ker\psi_G=(F_{ij}:i\ne j,\ i\leftrightarrow j\notin B)\) is prime, and \(R_{\mathrm{inc}}/I_G\cong R_{\mathrm{src}}\). Its covariance restriction has kernel \(P_G\), so \(R_G\cong\operatorname{im}\phi_G\), \(K_G=\operatorname{Frac}(R_G)\subseteq L\), and \(I_G:S_G^{\infty}=I_G\) for the exact multiplicative set \(S_G=R_{\sigma}\setminus P_G\). Consequently \(A_K=S_G^{-1}(R_{\mathrm{inc}}/I_G)\) is integral with fraction field \(L\), and covariance localization deletes no generic point or finite \(\lambda_e\)-value: if \(\lambda_e\) is algebraic, its affine coordinate image over \(\overline{K_G}\) is exactly the root set of its minimal polynomial, even when the full generic fiber is positive dimensional; if it is transcendental, the coordinate image is Zariski dense and infinite. No directed-coordinate expression is inverted, so poles and identically zero-over-zero components created by intermediate rational formulas remain in the incidence algebra. Homogenized elimination records projective-infinity points separately, while affine dehomogenization retains exactly the finite coordinate image; denominator zeros and leading-coefficient drops are specialization loci and do not change the generic affine image.
statements.justification: The explicit prime incidence algebra and covariance-only localization prevent coordinate branches from being silently removed during elimination.
statements.gap: Foygel, Draisma, and Drton factor full generic fibers, while the stated theorem identifies the exact covariance multiplicative set and preserves one coordinate through positive-dimensional fibers, poles, zero-over-zero components, and projective specialization.
statements.consumer: The minimal-polynomial routine can invert certified covariance-model classes while retaining every generic value of the requested coefficient and auditing every affine or projective exclusion.

statements.statement: For every \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\) with \(d_e(G)<\infty\), \[d_e(G)\le 2^{|D|-n+2}\le2^{k+1}.\] The first inequality holds even when the generic full parameter fiber is positive dimensional.
statements.justification: This gives the first universal parameterized ceiling for one algebraic edge coordinate beyond directed trees.
statements.gap: Existing tree-only identification theory and old higher-degree small SEM examples do not bound a single coordinate by excess-parent count.
statements.consumer: A fixed-parameter symbolic engine can allocate elimination degree and certificate storage before seeing numerical covariance values.

statements.statement: For every \(k\ge0\) and \(n\ge2k+4\), \(d_{e^{\star}}(G^{\star}_{k,n})=2^{k+1}\) and therefore \[D_k(n)=2^{k+1}.\] One original coefficient \(e^{\star}\) separates all branches on a nonempty Zariski-open covariance set.
statements.justification: A uniform attaining region turns the exponent from a loose Bezout count into a sharp coordinate frontier for a substantial size range.
statements.gap: Foygel, Draisma, and Drton already exhibit cubic and quartic behavior in small SEMs, but not an all-\(k\) family with one edge separating \(2^{k+1}\) generic branches.
statements.consumer: Software maintainers obtain adversarial benchmark families and users obtain a worst-case ambiguity warning indexed by the number of added parents.

statements.statement: The exact tree maxima are \(D_0(2)=D_0(3)=1\) and \(D_0(n)=2\) for \(n\ge4\). For \(n=2\), the sole missing-bidirected residual is either absent, giving a transcendental query, or linear in the unique edge coefficient. For \(n=3\), consider the star \(0\to1,0\to2\) and the chain \(0\to1\to2\). In either shape the parent--child residuals, when present, are linear anchors. The only remaining residual is bilinear in the two edge coefficients: alone it leaves each query transcendental, and after either linear anchor it solves the other coefficient linearly. The unconfounded chain supplies degree one. For \(n=4\), take the star \(0\to1,0\to2,0\to3\), include exactly the three bows \(0\leftrightarrow j\), and omit all three child--child bidirected edges. Writing \(a=\lambda_{01},b=\lambda_{02},c=\lambda_{03}\), its three residual equations are \(\sigma_{ij}-\lambda_{0i}\sigma_{0j}-\lambda_{0j}\sigma_{0i}+\lambda_{0i}\lambda_{0j}\sigma_{00}=0\) for \(1\le i<j\le3\). At the positive-definite source point \(a,b,c=(1,2,3)\), \(\omega_{00}=1\), \(\omega_{11}=\omega_{22}=\omega_{33}=10\), and \((\omega_{01},\omega_{02},\omega_{03})=(1/5,-1/7,1/11)\), elimination gives \((a-1)(5a-7)/385\). The roots lift to \((a,b,c)=(1,2,3)\) and \((7/5,12/7,35/11)\); the residual Jacobian determinants are respectively \(-2/385\) and \(2/385\), and the Möbius denominators are respectively \(-1/5\) and \(1/5\). Hence both branches are simple and pole-free. Appending fully bidirected children of \(0\) preserves the eliminant for every larger \(n\).
statements.justification: Explicit residual reductions and a pole-free quadratic witness supply the size-specific lower bounds; the matching ceiling is recorded as a bibliographic proof input.
statements.gap: This is an appendix boundary verification, not a new tree-classification claim; the field-tier novelty remains the positive-excess all-size frontier.
statements.consumer: The sharp recurrence receives verified \(k=0\) base values for every graph size.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf{FrontierHandle}\), determine an explicit formula or finite structural recurrence solely in \(n,k\) for \(D_k(n)\) at every admissible pair. Prove a universal upper bound equal to that recurrence, construct a graph-query family in \(\mathcal G_{n,k}\) attaining it for every pair, and prove that one original directed coefficient separates the retained generic branches. The recurrence must account for forced covariance relations, losses under the exact \(S_G\)-localization and affine dehomogenization, and roots at projective infinity, and must agree with the separately verified values in \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}maxima\mbox{-}support}\) at \(k=0\) and with \(2^{k+1}\) when \(n\ge2k+4\).
statements.justification: The all-size exact frontier, rather than another isolated higher-degree graph, is the theorem-level kernel.
statements.gap: The tree papers settle only \(k=0\), while Foygel, Draisma, and Drton compute small whole-fiber degrees; no source gives the maximum single-coordinate degree as a function of both size and excess-parent budget.
statements.consumer: The result supplies fasttreeid with an exact ambiguity budget and a sharp stop rule for every supported graph size.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf{CensusHandle}\), determine \(d_e(G)\) for every rooted graph-query orbit with \(n\le5\) and \(k\le2\) over characteristic zero. In particular, either certify the supplied five-vertex quartic in \(A_K=S_G^{-1}(R_{\mathrm{inc}}/I_G)\) or exhibit the first strict loss between the prescribed-orientation count and the SEM coordinate degree; any strict loss must be incorporated into the recurrence sought in \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}size\mbox{-}frontier}\).
statements.justification: This is the bounded destructive test that can invalidate the uncorrected orientation-realization conjecture before the all-size proof is attempted.
statements.gap: The five-node computations of Foygel, Draisma, and Drton classify whole graphs and selected whole-fiber degrees, not every original-edge coordinate degree under the rooted excess-arrow budget in the \(S_G\)-localized prime incidence algebra.
statements.consumer: The frontier proof receives certified base cases or a concrete correction term, and fasttreeid receives a complete small-instance regression suite.

statements.statement: For every \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\), the construction \(\mathsf{Core}_{G,e}\) uses at most \(2k\) exposed directed coefficients, has equations of degree at most two with rational-circuit coefficients in \(K_G\), records every pole and identically zero-over-zero interaction, and preserves exactly the finite or infinite projection degree of \(\lambda_e\).
statements.justification: This converts distance from a tree into a bounded-dimensional elimination problem without multiplying unrelated branch counts.
statements.gap: The Möbius reduction of Gupta and Bläser has one coefficient per vertex and relies on tree-specific rank-one behavior; the source-integral anchoring step is needed after extra parents couple components.
statements.consumer: The core is the exact symbolic intermediate representation needed to extend fasttreeid beyond one parent per node.

statements.statement: There is a universal \(C>0\) such that \(\mathsf A(G,T,e,\delta)\) first determines whether \(d_e(G)<\infty\). On the finite branch it returns exactly \((d_e(G),p_e,\mathcal Q_{G,e},h_{G,e})\), where \(p_e\in K_G[t]\) is monic with rational-circuit coefficients. On the transcendental branch it returns exactly \((\infty,\mathcal N_{G,e})\), where \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\) certifies that the queried-coordinate projection of a positive-dimensional irreducible generic-fiber component is dominant onto \(\mathbb A^1_{K_G}\), and it returns no \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\). In \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\), construction time and certificate length are at most \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\), and total symbolic error probability is at most \(\delta\). On the tree-plus-\(k\) class, the finite branch strictly strengthens the general polynomial-space yes-or-no procedure by returning the coordinate degree and eliminant.
statements.justification: A sharp degree frontier becomes operational only with a complete graph-input certificate of the queried minimal polynomial.
statements.gap: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma search bounded-degree rational formulas, and Dörfler et al. decide general identification in polynomial space; neither returns algebraic coordinate minimal polynomials with fixed-parameter certificates.
statements.consumer: fasttreeid can replace its \(0/1/2\) status by exact higher finite degree and a verifiable branch polynomial for added-parent graphs.

statements.statement: Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\). With probability at least \(1-\delta\), \(h_{G,e}\) is not the zero polynomial and \(\mathcal E_{G,e}\) is proper. For every complex covariance specialization \(\Sigma\notin\mathcal E_{G,e}\) in the model image, \[\{z\in\mathbb C:p_e(\Sigma,z)=0\}=\mathcal Z_e(G,\Sigma).\] This equality uses the specialized prime incidence ideal \(I_G\) and remains valid when its full \(\Lambda\)-fiber is positive dimensional. The circuits in \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\) certify that every coordinate-preserving slice meets every generic finite branch, intermediate poles and identically zero-over-zero components are retained or lifted back to \(I_G\), the specialized leading coefficient does not drop, and no finite root is exchanged with a root at projective infinity. The roots are distinct whenever the squarefreeness circuit is nonzero.
statements.justification: The exceptional set makes the word generic auditable and excludes poles, lost leading terms, and infinity components explicitly.
statements.gap: Generic RUR specialization theory supplies general bad loci, but no existing result packages \(S_G\)-localization of the prime SEM incidence ideal and single-edge projection into a causal graph certificate.
statements.consumer: Users can test whether an observed or simulated covariance lies inside the certified operating region before interpreting polynomial roots.

statements.statement: Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\). For every regular real \(\Sigma\succ0\) outside \(\mathcal E_{G,e}\), the algorithm returns \(\mathsf{LiftCert}\) for each simple real root \(z\) of \(p_e(\Sigma,\cdot)\), and \(\mathsf{LiftCert}\) accepts if and only if \(z\in\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\). For every accepted complete real supported \(\Lambda\), the recovered matrix \(\Omega=(I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_n-\Lambda)\) is positive definite by congruence; positivity of \(\Omega\) is a conclusion and is not an antecedent of the lifting criterion.
statements.justification: Complex degree is not a real ambiguity count, so root-by-root extension is required before a causal coefficient value is reported.
statements.gap: Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant separate real positive-definite fibers from complex genericity, and Bouzidi et al. isolate real solutions; the missing result is an if-and-only-if supported-SEM lift for each projected coordinate root.
statements.consumer: Applied SEM analysts receive all and only real structural explanations of a regular observed covariance, without a false uniqueness conclusion from local rank.

statements.statement: Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\) and the certificate event on which \(h_{G,e}\) is nonzero. The real supported source set \(\{(\Lambda,\Omega):\Lambda\in\mathbb R^D,\ \Omega\succ0,\ \Omega_{ij}=0\text{ if }i\leftrightarrow j\notin B\}\) is Euclidean open in its support space and Zariski dense in the complex source space. Since \(\mathcal E_{G,e}\) is proper on the model image, there is a real supported source point \((\Lambda_0,\Omega_0)\) whose covariance \(\Sigma_0\) lies in \(\mathcal M_G\setminus\mathcal E_{G,e}\). A smooth semialgebraic stratification refined by the real-lifting sign conditions contains \(\Sigma_0\) in a connected cell \(\mathcal C_{G,e}\) on which real-extension status is constant, and a sufficiently small closed chart ball gives a nonempty compact \(\mathcal K_G\subset\mathcal C_{G,e}\) with nonempty relative interior. For every \(\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G\), \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\ne\varnothing\), because membership in \(\mathcal M_G\) supplies at least one complete real supported \(\Lambda\).
statements.justification: The regular statistical domain must be shown nonvacuous and its real identified set must be nonempty rather than imposed by assumption.
statements.gap: Standard stratification arguments isolate smooth cells, but the stated lemma ties such a cell to the certified SEM exceptional locus and to rootwise real extension.
statements.consumer: The inference theorem obtains a genuine compact operating region and a nonempty target set on every data-generating covariance in that region.

statements.statement: Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\). On \(\mathcal K_G\), every nonzero denominator, specialized-leading-coefficient, and squarefreeness factor in \(h_{G,e}\) has a positive minimum in absolute value by continuity and compactness. Hence every rational-circuit coefficient of the finite monic polynomial \(p_e\) is uniformly bounded, and the monic Cauchy bound confines all \(d_e(G)\) complex roots to one fixed disk. The root-incidence set over \(\mathcal K_G\) is compact; because the squarefreeness factor does not vanish, \(\partial_t p_e\) has a positive minimum in absolute value on that set. Consequently there is \(\gamma>0\) such that every two distinct complex roots, and therefore every two distinct retained real roots, are separated by at least \(\gamma\), uniformly over \(\mathcal K_G\).
statements.justification: Denominator, derivative, and branch-separation margins follow from the certified exceptional locus and compactness, so none is imposed as a free condition.
statements.gap: Standard simple-root perturbation results often posit isolated roots; this lemma records the compact polynomial argument that produces the isolation margin for the certified SEM eliminant.
statements.consumer: The finite-set matching and simultaneous branch neighborhoods use derived regularity constants without narrowing the statistical class by an oracle margin assumption.

statements.statement: Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\). There are events \(\mathcal H_m\) with \(\inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}\Pr_{\Sigma}(\mathcal H_m)\to1\) such that, on \(\mathcal H_m\), \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}\) is nonempty and is bijectively matched to \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\). With the empty-set convention in \(d_H\), uniformly over \(\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G\), \(d_H(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m},\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma))=O_{\mathbb P}(m^{-1/2})\) and \(\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}\Pr_{\Sigma}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\varnothing)\to0\). Under local branch labels, \[\sqrt m\{r(\pi_G(S_m))-r(\Sigma)\}\rightsquigarrow N\!\left(0,Dr(\Sigma)D\pi_G(\Sigma)V_\Sigma D\pi_G(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}Dr(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}\right),\] and the simultaneous neighborhoods \(\mathcal A_m\) cover every retained branch with asymptotic probability \(1-\alpha\), uniformly on \(\mathcal K_G\).
statements.justification: The observationally equivalent branches are the estimand, so inference must cover them simultaneously rather than select one.
statements.gap: Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer treat general criterion-defined sets, while Mareis, Sturma, and Drton derive regular half-trek point inference; neither gives root-specific joint inference for a finite algebraic SEM coordinate fiber.
statements.consumer: Researchers using a graph with added parents can report sampling uncertainty around every compatible direct-effect branch.

statements.statement: Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\). If \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)=\{r_1(\Sigma)\}\) on \(\mathcal K_G\), then with probability tending to one uniformly on \(\mathcal K_G\), \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}\) has exactly one element; that element is consistent and asymptotically normal with the scalar variance given by the corresponding diagonal entry of the covariance matrix in \(\mathrm{thm:regular\mbox{-}finite\mbox{-}set\mbox{-}inference}\).
statements.justification: The singleton case connects finite-set inference to the familiar direct-effect estimator and Wald limit.
statements.gap: Regular half-trek asymptotic normality covers rationally identified coefficients, whereas this corollary also covers a singleton real projection of a higher complex-degree coordinate polynomial.
statements.consumer: When only one real supported branch survives, applied users obtain an ordinary point estimate, standard error, and confidence interval.

sampling_model.design: The identification layer uses the exact population covariance of a known recursive Gaussian mixed graph. The estimation layer uses independent observational sampling at fixed \(G,n\).
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the causal query is the direct structural coefficient \(\lambda_e\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: When \(d_e(G)<\infty\), project \(S_m\) smoothly onto the regular covariance-model stratum, evaluate the certificate circuits and \(p_e\), isolate every simple real root, and retain roots by exact local real-extension status. When \(d_e(G)=\infty\), the symbolic stage reports transcendence and the finite-set inference rung does not apply.

estimand_functional: \(D_k(n)=\max_{(G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k},\ d_e(G)<\infty}[K_G(\lambda_e):K_G]\), with finite fibers represented by \(p_e(t)\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: TreeID introduced the missing-bidirected-cycle method for tree-shaped linear SEMs; the 2022 paper did not itself prove completeness, while Gupta--Bläser later established the complete per-edge \(1/2/\infty\) classification and Briefs--Bläser explicitly reports TreeID as complete in light of that result.
Theorem 27 gives the complete per-parameter \(1/2/\infty\) trichotomy for rooted directed trees and therefore the finite-degree upper boundary two.
Theorem 1 gives an \(O(n^3\log^2 n)\) randomized implementation of the same complete tree-only \(1/2/\infty\) predicate.
The paper gives polynomial-time sufficient and necessary-side graphical criteria, full-fiber mixed-component decomposition, and small-graph finite-degree computations.
Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.4 transfer rational identification of coefficients from ancestral induced subgraphs to the full graph.
Corollary 6 places generic edge identifiability in polynomial space without returning an algebraic coordinate eliminant.
Theorems 4.4 and 5.1 search for minimum bounded-degree rational identifying formulas and give quasi-polynomial computation for a fixed formula-degree bound.
Theorem 2.1 constructs a generic rational univariate representation for generically zero-dimensional parametric polynomial systems and later results control specialization outside explicit bad loci.
The paper computes separating forms, rational univariate representations, isolating boxes, and exact signs for bivariate polynomial systems.
The paper derives consistency, rates, and confidence regions for criterion-defined identified sets by sample-criterion inversion.
The preprint derives influence functions, asymptotic normality, and Wald inference for rational half-trek estimators.
The paper distinguishes global real identifiability from generic algebraic behavior and analyzes explicit degree-two failures of injectivity.

tldr: Adding a bounded number of parents to a supplied rooted directed tree creates a finite algebraic ambiguity regime not summarized by whole-fiber cardinality. The focal object is the sharp single-coordinate complex degree frontier \(D_k(n)\). The project derives the exact frontier for every size and excess-edge budget through a projection-aware orientation-realization recurrence, proves the universal \(2^{k+1}\) ceiling and an attaining one-sink family for \(n\ge2k+4\), and turns the proof into a fixed-parameter minimal-polynomial and exceptional-set certificate. A separate real lifting test filters complex roots, and regular finite-set inference estimates every retained branch at the root-\(m\) rate without branch selection.

project_justification.gap: Existing tree algorithms and general mixed-graph work study identification decisions, rational recovery, whole-parameter fibers, or unparameterized elimination. No result determines the maximum finite extension degree of one directed coefficient as a function of both graph size and the number of extra parents.
project_justification.niche: Distance from a supplied arborescence creates a parameterized algebraic regime in which ordinary vertices retain Möbius structure while at most \(2k\) exceptional incoming coefficients form a coupled quadratic core. The hard boundary is whether constrained covariance coefficients realize the multihomogeneous orientation count at every smaller size.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves a projection-aware upper bound, constructs branch-separating graph families, resolves the all-size orientation-realization recurrence, and supplies minimal-polynomial, exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference guarantees in the output format required by an extension of fasttreeid.

related_work: Van der Zander, Wienöbst, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz introduced TreeID for tree-shaped linear SEMs: the 2022 paper developed the missing-bidirected-cycle method and a polynomial-space procedure, but did not itself prove completeness. Gupta and Bläser later established the complete per-parameter \(1/2/\infty\) classification through rank-one anchoring, Möbius propagation, cycle closure, and polynomial identity testing; that result is used solely as the cited \(k=0\) boundary, while the sharp-size question begins at positive excess-arrow budget. Briefs and Bläser explicitly report TreeID as complete in light of the later Gupta--Bläser result, accelerate the tree predicate, and implement it in fasttreeid; the proposed algorithm enlarges its graph and symbolic-output domain, without claiming a better \(k=0\) running time. The novelty claim is reserved for finite single-coordinate degrees beyond this tree trichotomy. Foygel, Draisma, and Drton develop half-trek criteria, factor whole generic fibers across mixed components, and exhibit higher-degree small SEMs, which makes a lone cubic or quartic non-novel and motivates the single-coordinate projection distinction. Drton and Weihs show that ancestral subgraphs can identify individual coefficients, but their reduction stops at rational identification rather than extension degree. Dörfler, van der Zander, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz give a complete polynomial-space generic edge decision procedure; the fixed-parameter theorem strengthens its output on the tree-plus-\(k\) class to the exact degree, minimal polynomial, and bad-locus certificate. Hollering, Misra, and Sturma optimize bounded-degree rational formulas, a different degree notion from algebraic branch degree. Corniquel, Jeronimo and Sabia, Emiris, and Bouzidi et al. provide generic RUR, circuit-resultant, sparse-elimination, and real-isolation machinery that informs the certificate construction but does not prove covariance-residual sparsity or coordinate preservation. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer provide the identified-set inference architecture, Drton diagnoses nonstandard behavior at singularities, and Mareis, Sturma, and Drton derive regular half-trek influence functions; the statistical rung is restricted to separated simple algebraic branches and makes no discriminant-uniform claim.
technical_internal_limitation: The orientation coefficient is only an upper envelope until covariance-coefficient relations, \(S_G\)-localization, affine dehomogenization, and projective infinity are controlled. The rooted five-node characteristic-zero census is the explicit kill test: a strict loss must alter the all-size recurrence rather than be hidden by the large-size family. The modular quartic and the degree-eight and degree-sixteen rational checks are evidence, not statements. Coordinate-preserving localization must never be promoted to equality of full fibers. Real roots are never equated with real supported lifts, and local Jacobian rank is never used to claim real uniqueness.
honest_scope: All formal nodes are to be proved. The all-\(n\) recurrence and attaining families are the open kernel; the large-size exponent is supporting traction and cannot replace it. The algorithmic theorem must cost every slice, \(S_G\)-localization, incidence lift, affine dehomogenization, coefficient descent, circuit gate, and identity-test error. On a transcendental query it returns exactly \((\infty,\mathcal N_{G,e})\) and no minimal polynomial or polynomial-dependent exceptional-set object. Statistical inference is confined to fixed finite-degree queries and nonempty compact subsets of smooth connected real-model cells outside the certified exceptional set, with locally constant real-extension status. Certificate-denominator, simple-root derivative, and branch-separation margins are conclusions of compactness, continuity, monic Cauchy bounds, and the squarefreeness factor in \(h_{G,e}\), not assumptions. The finite-sample estimator may be empty off its validity event, but its emptiness probability vanishes uniformly and Hausdorff loss uses the explicit empty-set convention. No inference uniform over discriminants, no automatic branch selection, and no all-singular-covariance guarantee is claimed. Positive definiteness of a recovered disturbance matrix follows by congruence from a complete real supported lift and positive-definite \(\Sigma\). Separate explicit residual checks supply the exact small-size maxima. The singleton real-fiber reduction yields ordinary asymptotic normality.

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, Sections 4--8, especially Lemmas 7--8, 12--13, 25, Theorem 27, and the final running-time discussion
seed_details.opportunity: Determine \(D_k(n)\) exactly for every admissible size and excess-arrow budget, with a universal coordinate-degree upper bound and attaining graph-query families.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace scalar Möbius cycle closure by a coordinate-transcendence-basis freeze and a blockwise multihomogeneous orientation count at the first vertex with a second parent.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Searches for linear-SEM single-coordinate field degree, tree-plus-extra-edge degree, and excess-parent Bezout bounds found the tree predicate, general fiber computations, and unrelated multihomogeneous orientation counts, but no occupied target--method pair.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may say the result is immediate from the tree quadratic bound by multiplying one factor of two per extra edge.
seed_details.rebuttal: Independent multiplication counts joint branches, whereas distinct joint solutions can share \(\lambda_e\); positive-dimensional fibers, forced covariance relations, \(S_G\)-localization, and roots at infinity make both the upper bound and every-size attainment nonformal.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed uses the structure-identification motif M18 with generic-class sharpness M7, not a do-calculus effect-identification framing; the focal object is the explicit frontier \(D_k(n)\).

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, Example 8, Section 8 on acyclic mixed-component decomposition, the proof of the degree factorization, and Section 10 Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Give exact max, product, or subfield-intersection rules for \([K_G(\lambda_e):K_G]\) under mixed-component and ancestral reductions.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: At the full-fiber multiplication step, retain the image of the single coordinate and compute stabilizers or subfield intersections before multiplying component degrees.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Searches pairing mixed-component decomposition with coordinate projection degree found individual-edge rational criteria and whole-fiber factorization, but no higher-degree projection theorem.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may claim coordinate degree is automatically the degree of the mixed component containing the queried edge.
seed_details.rebuttal: Branches inside that component can collide after coordinate projection, and extra parents can couple components over a nontrivial covariance subfield, so the equality needs a necessary-and-sufficient field-intersection argument.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is an iff structural theorem rather than an analogue on a self-defined subclass.

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, Theorems 4.4 and 5.1 with their circuit-enumeration proofs, and the concluding limitations on fixed rational formula degree
seed_details.opportunity: Return the exact algebraic coordinate degree, monic minimal polynomial, and a checkable exceptional-set certificate in \(n^{O(k+1)}\) time.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace enumeration of bounded-degree rational formulas by source-integral Möbius reduction to a \(2k\)-variable quadratic core and coordinate multiplication on a preserving slice.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Searches for SEM minimal-polynomial algorithms, algebraic edge-degree certificates, and parametric RURs found general RUR and rational-identification algorithms but no tree-distance fixed-parameter result.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may regard the theorem as a direct call to generic elimination or a generic RUR package.
seed_details.rebuttal: Generic elimination gives neither the \(n^{O(k+1)}\) bound nor coordinate preservation on positive-dimensional fibers, coefficient descent to \(K_G\), explicit \(S_G\)-localization and incidence-lifting circuits, or a global symbolic error budget.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed has a named certificate algorithm and an exact complexity guarantee; black-box eliminability is expressly not the claim.

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, Example 8, Section 7.1 exhaustive computations through five vertices, and Section 10 Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Produce a characteristic-zero census in \(S_G^{-1}(R_{\mathrm{inc}}/I_G)\) for every rooted \(n\le5\), \(k\le2\) graph-query orbit and isolate every loss from its orientation envelope.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Refine the small-graph Gröbner computation from generic identifiability and whole-fiber degree to the affine eliminant of each original directed coordinate in \(S_G^{-1}(R_{\mathrm{inc}}/I_G)\), with projective-infinity points tracked separately.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: The five-node literature reports graph-level criteria and selected full degrees; no retrieved census records every queried-coordinate extension degree with arborescence and excess-arrow labels.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may dismiss the project as a finite database with no theorem beyond computer algebra.
seed_details.rebuttal: The census is valuable as the mandated kill test and recurrence base, but it is insufficient as the main paper and is therefore folded into the selected frontier program.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is not elevated above subfield ambition and is retained only as a falsification and base-case module.

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, the sparse resultant construction and complexity theorem, the coefficient-genericity discussion, and the concluding algorithmic section
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize exactly which prescribed-indegree orientation counts are realizable by SEM covariance residual coefficients without loss to infinity or forced relations.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace freely variable sparse-system coefficients by the constrained covariance-coefficient map and prove dominance or quantify its image defect before invoking a mixed-volume count.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Searches joining SEM covariance residuals, orientation counts, multihomogeneous Bezout, and sparse-resultant sharpness found analogous rigidity counts but no covariance-realization theorem.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may say generic coefficients make the multihomogeneous Bezout number sharp by standard sparse elimination.
seed_details.rebuttal: SEM residual coefficients lie on a constrained image of the covariance parametrization; the five-node modular probe exists precisely because genericity in the ambient coefficient space does not transfer automatically.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed demands necessity and sufficiency over a nonempty generic region, not a single tuned witness.

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, the global-identifiability theorem and degree-two cycle proof, examples separating real and generic behavior, and Discussion
seed_details.opportunity: Give a necessary-and-sufficient semialgebraic certificate for whether each simple real coordinate root extends to a real supported coefficient matrix.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After computing the coordinate eliminant, replace root counting by root-indexed RUR lifts to the prime incidence ideal \(I_G\) and exact sign evaluation of every missing-bidirected residual.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Searches for real algebraic SEM branch lifting and coordinate-root feasibility found global injectivity theory and general RUR isolation, but no root-by-root supported-SEM criterion.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may assert that every real root of a real minimal polynomial automatically yields a real SEM parameter vector.
seed_details.rebuttal: A real coordinate of a complex fiber need not have a fully real lift; positive definiteness follows only after a complete real supported \(\Lambda\) has been recovered.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed states an iff lifting criterion and never equates complex degree, real root count, local rank, or real uniqueness.

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, the set-estimator consistency and rate theorems, confidence-region inversion, and Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Estimate every simple separated real algebraic branch with root-\(m\) Hausdorff rate, a joint Gaussian limit, and simultaneous branch neighborhoods.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a general sample-criterion level set by the implicit root map of the certified coordinate polynomial after smooth covariance-model projection.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Searches for finite algebraic identified-set inference in linear SEMs found general set inference, singularity warnings, and rational half-trek influence functions, but no exhaustive regular branch CLT.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may call the result a routine delta method for polynomial roots.
seed_details.rebuttal: The theorem must couple feasible covariance projection, exhaustive branch matching, locally constant real-extension filtering, Hausdorff loss, and simultaneous joint coverage; it is secondary because collisions remain excluded.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The rate and joint limit are attached to the exact-identification shape as an M8 rung; the seed is not mislabeled as bare M8 and makes no singular-uniform claim.

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, Theorem 2.1 and its Van der Waerden resultant proof, Section 4.3 specialization results, and Sections 4.6--5.3
seed_details.opportunity: Compile every covariance-localization failure, incidence-lifting failure, pole, projective leading-form loss, specialized leading-coefficient drop, repeated root, and real-lift boundary into a proper circuit-defined covariance exceptional set.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a generically zero-dimensional parametric ideal by a positive-dimensional generic SEM fiber sliced only after proving that every conjugate queried-coordinate value survives localization.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: The exact target--method search found general specialization loci for RURs but no causal coordinate certificate preserving projections of positive-dimensional covariance fibers.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may say the bad locus is simply the discriminant of the eliminant.
seed_details.rebuttal: A discriminant does not exclude deleted poles, zero-over-zero components, leading-coefficient drops, roots at infinity, or failure of a real coordinate root to lift through the original residual system.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed names an evaluable bad-locus circuit rather than invoking genericity without a certificate.

candidate_scans.anchor_read: Gupta and Bläser move from the general identification problem to the rooted-tree restriction in the Introduction, encode rank-two residuals as Möbius maps in Sections 4--5, prove that an identifying cycle gives the full one-coordinate solution count in Lemmas 12--13, handle rank-one anchors in Lemma 25, and assemble the complete \(1/2/\infty\) algorithm in Theorem 27. The adapted proof begins exactly where a second parent changes a scalar variable into a block.
adjacent_threads: Van der Zander, Wienöbst, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz introduced the AISTATS 2022 TreeID predecessor and its missing-bidirected-cycle method without themselves proving completeness; Gupta and Bläser's Theorem 27 later established the complete per-edge trichotomy, and Briefs and Bläser explicitly report TreeID as complete in light of that result.
Foygel, Draisma, and Drton, Example 8 and Section 7.1, establish that higher finite whole-fiber degrees already occur and therefore rule out isolated cubic or quartic examples as novelty.
Briefs and Bläser, Theorem 1 and Appendix B, retain the same tree classification while reducing identity-testing cost and exposing the fasttreeid consumer interface.
Drton and Weihs, Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.4, show how ancestral restriction preserves rational recovery of corresponding edges but do not track algebraic coordinate degree.

Bartzos, Emiris, and Schicho relate multihomogeneous Bezout coefficients to prescribed orientation counts in a different constrained polynomial system, supporting the combinatorial handle while warning that exactness is model-dependent.
candidate_scans.settled: The exact \(k=0\) trichotomy, general higher-degree existence, whole-fiber decomposition, and the universal meaning of multihomogeneous orientation counts are settled.
candidate_scans.unoccupied_pair: No retrieved paper determines single-edge extension degree over all rooted tree-plus-\(k\) mixed graphs or attains a size-sensitive maximum for every \(n,k\).
candidate_scans.subsumption_check: The closest later work accelerates the tree predicate or studies rational formulas; neither subsumes the algebraic coordinate frontier.

candidate_scans.anchor_read: Foygel, Draisma, and Drton formulate generic and rational identifiability in the Introduction, exhibit finite degrees in Example 8, and use Tian mixed-component decomposition in Section 8; the proof multiplies full generic fiber degrees. The proposed adaptation changes that multiplication step by passing to a single coordinate image and its subfield intersections.
adjacent_threads: Drton and Weihs prove ancestral transfer for individual rationally identified edges, but their argument only pulls back a rational formula.
Weihs et al. isolate individual edges using determinantal instrumental variables, again only at degree one.

Gupta and Bläser show within a tree rank-two component that total component solutions equal the solutions of one coordinate, a special projection-preservation fact unavailable after extra-parent coupling.
candidate_scans.settled: Whole-fiber degree multiplication and rational single-edge recovery under sufficient graphical conditions are settled.
candidate_scans.unoccupied_pair: No exact projection-aware degree rule under mixed-component or ancestral decomposition was found.
candidate_scans.subsumption_check: Ancestor decomposition is not closer because it proves only sufficiency for rational recovery and supplies no field-degree equality or necessity direction.

candidate_scans.anchor_read: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma motivate bounded symbolic output in the Introduction and enumerate candidate rational identifying formulas in Theorems 4.4 and 5.1. The adapted move replaces formula enumeration by a causal-sparsity reduction to a bounded quadratic core and computes a coordinate minimal polynomial rather than a rational expression.
adjacent_threads: Dörfler et al. give general polynomial-space decision procedures and hardness but do not output finite algebraic branches.
Corniquel, Theorem 2.1 and Section 4.3, constructs generic RURs and specialization loci for generically zero-dimensional parametric systems.
Jeronimo and Sabia compute multihomogeneous resultants by straight-line programs with complexity controlled by the resultant degree.
Bouzidi et al. compute separating forms, RURs, isolating boxes, and signs, supplying the real-lifting backend after the causal reduction.
candidate_scans.settled: General exact elimination, generic RUR specialization, circuit-valued multihomogeneous resultants, and bounded-degree rational formula search are settled in their respective settings.
candidate_scans.unoccupied_pair: No source proves an \(n^{O(k+1)}\) algorithm for algebraic single-edge degree and minimal-polynomial certificates in tree-plus-\(k\) covariance models.
candidate_scans.subsumption_check: Corniquel assumes a generically zero-dimensional parametric system, whereas the SEM full fiber may be positive dimensional and only the coordinate projection is finite; this prevents direct subsumption.

literature_map.writing_exemplar_used: GuptaBlaser2024TreeSCM, Introduction and Theorem 27: general identification difficulty, a transparent graph restriction, a complete per-edge ambiguity classification, and an explicit symbolic algorithmic output.
method_exemplars_used: GuptaBlaser2024TreeSCM, Lemmas 7--8, 12--13, 25, and Theorem 27 for rank-one anchoring, Möbius propagation, cycle closure, and source-parameter polynomial identity testing.
FoygelDraismaDrton2012HTC, Example 8, Section 7.1, and Section 8 for higher finite degrees, small-graph algebra, and full-fiber mixed-component decomposition.
Corniquel2026GenericRUR, Theorem 2.1 and Section 4.3 for generic RUR construction and specialization control.
JeronimoSabia2007MultihomogeneousResultant for circuit-valued resultants, and ChernozhukovHongTamer2007SetInference for Hausdorff set estimation and confidence-region inversion.
literature_map.target_method_occupancy: The occupied adjacent numerical proposal studies a supplied-covariance real singleton predicate with a growing number of two-parent vertices. The present kernel instead fixes the complex function field, maximizes a single-coordinate algebraic degree over every size and excess budget, and requires sharp attainment and generic certificates. The numerical residual handle is used only as non-novel supporting machinery.
literature_map.candidate_dispositions: The sharp frontier, projection-aware decomposition, and fixed-parameter minimal-polynomial candidates survived deepening. The five-node census and orientation-realization theorem are necessary modules of the selected frontier rather than standalone papers. Real lifting and regular inference remain secondary rungs. Exceptional specialization is folded into the symbolic theorem.
